newsitem.title: USA: Drug not helpful for stroke victims, study says.
newsitem.headline: Drug not helpful for stroke victims, study says.

text.p: The blood clot-dissolving drug streptokinase is not helpful for stroke victims and may cause complications if given more than three hours after a stroke, researchers reported on Tuesday.

A study involving 340 patients designed to test the efficacy of the drug in treating stroke was halted because of unacceptably high complication rates, according to researchers from the Austin and Repatriation Medical Centre, Heidelberg, Victoria, Australia.

Patients given the drug was within three hours of a stroke fared virtually the same as stroke victims not given the drug, said the report published in this week's Journal of the American Medical Association.

When streptokinase, which is often used for treating heart attacks, was given to stroke victims more than three hours after a stroke occurred there was an increase in death rates beyond what would be expected, the report said.

Commenting on the study in an editorial in the same publication, Vladimir Hachinski of the University of Western Ontario in London, Ontario, said all major stroke tests with the drug "have been stopped early because of unacceptably high complication rates, and thus streptokinase cannot be recommended at this time for the treatment of acute stroke."
